drivingQuestion: Why is one who stole and slaughtered on Yom Kippur liable to pay, when that act incurs lashes?
outcomeNote: The difficulty is answered in the next unit (הא מני רבי מאיר)

segments.he: גָּנַב וְטָבַח בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וְכוּ׳. אָמְרִי: אַמַּאי? נְהִי דִּקְטָלָא לֵיכָּא, מַלְקוֹת מִיהָא אִיכָּא – וְקַיְימָא לַן דְּאֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה וּמְשַׁלֵּם!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If one «stole» an animal «and slaughtered» it «on Yom Kippur» he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment. The Sages «say,» questioning this ruling: «Why» is he liable to pay it? «Although there is no» penalty of «execution» for slaughtering on Yom Kippur, «nevertheless there is» the penalty of «lashes; and we maintain that» one «is not» sentenced to be «flogged and» obligated to «pay» for the same act.
